product_tiers.notes: OAuth app creation requires login to Notion Developers portal and workspace admin rights.

summary: Notion OAuth apps are created in the Notion Developer portal, require a logged‑in workspace owner, and use standard OAuth 2.0 endpoints; there is no public self‑serve registration page, and review details are not publicly documented.

time.setup_notes: Setup time varies; requires creating an integration, configuring redirect URIs, and copying client credentials.

approval_wait.label: None for basic install · Marketplace: not published
approval_wait.notes: Notion does not publish an OAuth app review or approval timeline.

prerequisites.notes: A personal or workspace account is needed to access the developer portal.

steps.title: Log in to Notion Developer portal
steps.detail: Navigate to https://developers.notion.com and sign in with a Notion account that has workspace owner permissions.

steps.title: Create a new integration
steps.detail: In the portal, click “Create new integration”, give it a name, select the workspace, and save. The integration page will display a client ID and client secret.

steps.title: Configure redirect URIs
steps.detail: Add one or more HTTPS redirect URIs (or http://localhost for testing) in the integration settings.

steps.title: Implement authorization request
steps.detail: Redirect users to https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, and optional scopes.

steps.title: Exchange code for access token
steps.detail: POST to https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token with grant_type=authorization_code, code, redirect_uri, and a Basic Authorization header containing base64‑encoded client_id:client_secret.

steps.title: Store and use the access token
steps.detail: Save the returned access token and include it as a Bearer token in API requests to Notion endpoints.

agent_can_do: Verify endpoint availability via HTTP GET
developer_must_do: Implement OAuth flow according to Notion docs

claims_evidence.claim: The OAuth token endpoint is https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token.
Development mode allows up to 1,000 users and tokens expire after 60 days.
Composio-managed OAuth is available for Notion.

composio_managed_auth.notes: Developer can start with Composio-managed OAuth; own app needed only for production branding, custom scopes or rate limits.
